metadata.name: Paul's Journey to Rome
metadata.description: Paul's voyage as a prisoner to Rome (~59-60 AD)

properties.name: Caesarea Maritima
properties.description: Paul, in the custody of a centurion named Julius, boarded a ship with other prisoners. Aristarchus from Thessalonica was with him.

properties.name: Sidon
properties.description: At Sidon, Julius treated Paul kindly and allowed him to visit his friends to be refreshed.

properties.name: Myra, Lycia
properties.description: At Myra the centurion found an Alexandrian ship sailing for Italy and put Paul and the prisoners on it.

properties.name: Fair Havens, Crete
properties.description: Paul warned them: 'I see that the voyage will be with injury and much loss, not only of the cargo and ship, but also of our lives.' The centurion trusted the pilot over Paul.

properties.name: Malta (Melita)
properties.description: The ship ran aground and broke apart in the storm. All 276 people escaped safely to Malta. Paul was bitten by a viper but unharmed. He healed the father of Publius and many others. They wintered there three months.

properties.name: Syracuse, Sicily
properties.description: They put in at Syracuse and stayed three days before continuing northward toward Rome.

properties.name: Puteoli (Pozzuoli)
properties.description: At Puteoli they found brothers who invited Paul to stay with them for seven days. And so Paul came to Rome.

properties.name: Rome
properties.description: Paul lived in his own rented house under guard, welcoming all who came to him. He preached the Kingdom of God and taught about the Lord Jesus Christ — boldly and without hindrance.
